preamble: Cairene Egyptian Arabic pronounces jīm (ج), /d͡ʒ/ in Standard Arabic and most dialects, as the velar stop [ɡ], even in Literary Arabic (ǧabal 'mountain' [ˈɡæbæl]). Whether this is a retention of Proto-Semitic *g or a later de-affrication is disputed. Following Blanc and Hary, scholars of Judaeo-Arabic date the stabilization of [ɡ] in Cairo to as late as 1800–1860, while many Arabic dialectologists treat [ɡ] as an archaism; Connolly (2019) argues that the Judaeo-Arabic spelling evidence for the late date is weaker than assumed. Only under the de-affrication view does this cell describe a real change.

examples.note: Cairene [ɡ] is used in colloquial and Literary Arabic alike; its origin as an innovation rather than a retention is debated.

sources: Connolly, M. M. (2019). Revisiting the Question of Ğīm from the Perspective of Judaeo-Arabic. Journal of Semitic Studies, 64(1), 155–183. https://doi.org/10.1093/jss/fgy033
